intent: Specify the civil time-of-day API of `jiff_core::civil::time`: `Time::new`, the `civil::time` constructor, the accessors `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `subsec_nanosecond`, `millisecond`, `microsecond`, `nanosecond`, the builders `with_subsec_parts` and `with_subsec_nanosecond`, the conversions `to_second` / `to_nanosecond`, `Time::on`, the derived `Ord`/`PartialEq` of `Time`, and the companion types `TimeSecond` (`new`, `constant`, `second`, `to_time`, `Ord`) and `TimeNanosecond` (`new`, `nanosecond`, `to_time`, `Ord`). Lean names live under `civil.time.Time`, `civil.time.TimeSecond`, `civil.time.TimeNanosecond` (field accessors are `….impl.hour` etc., trait methods `….Insts.CoreCmpOrd.cmp` / `….Insts.CoreCmpPartialEqTime.eq`). `bounds.RangeError` has no `DecidableEq`/`Repr`: inspect `core.result.Result` values by pattern matching.

manual_mutants.note: century rule: years divisible by 100 use %100 instead of %400 (1900-02-29 accepted)
days_in_month bit trick drops the >>3 fold: August..December get the wrong length
Date::new only consults days_in_month above day 29 (Feb 29 accepted in common years)
TimeNanosecond::to_time drops the sub-second part when the second component is 0
Ord ignores the sub-second component (inconsistent with Eq, not chronological)
with_subsec_parts forgets to scale microseconds by 1000
Time::new validates the hour with the minute bound (hours 24..=59 accepted)
microsecond() returns the total microseconds of the sub-second part (no % 1000)

sibling_mutants.note: Time::new validates the sub-second component first (different error reported when several components are invalid)
sibling_mutants.after: let r ← (do let rs ← bounds.SubsecNanosecond.checkc (IScalar.cast .I64 subsec_nanosecond); match rs with | core.result.Result.Ok _ => bounds.Hour.checkc i | core.result.Result.Err e => ok (core.result.Result.Err e))

sibling_mutants.note: with_subsec_parts validates the nanosecond part first
sibling_mutants.after: let r ← (do let rs ← bounds.Nanosecond.checkc (IScalar.cast .I64 nanosecond); match rs with | core.result.Result.Ok _ => bounds.Millisecond.checkc i | core.result.Result.Err e => ok (core.result.Result.Err e))

bug_variants.note: pre-fix Date::new only rejects days above 28 that exceed the month length and never checks `day < 1`, so `Time::on(y, m, 0)` (or a negative day) returns a DateTime with an impossible date instead of panicking as documented ('the day must be at least 1')

edits.with_text:
def civil.date.Date.new
  (year : Std.I16) (month : Std.I8) (day : Std.I8) :
  RustM (core.result.Result civil.date.Date bounds.RangeError)
  := do
  let i ← lift (IScalar.cast .I64 year)
  let r ← bounds.Year.checkc i
  match r with
  | core.result.Result.Ok val =>
    let i1 ← lift (IScalar.cast .I64 month)
    let r1 ← bounds.Month.checkc i1
    match r1 with
    | core.result.Result.Ok val1 =>
      if day > 28#i8
      then
        let i2 ← civil.days_in_month val val1
        if day > i2
        then
          let re ←
            bounds.SpecialBoundsError.into_range_error
              (bounds.SpecialBoundsError.DateInvalidDay val val1)
          ok (core.result.Result.Err re)
        else ok (core.result.Result.Ok { year := val, month := val1, day })
      else ok (core.result.Result.Ok { year := val, month := val1, day })
    | core.result.Result.Err err =>
      let re ← bounds.BoundsError.into_range_error err
      ok (core.result.Result.Err re)
  | core.result.Result.Err err =>
    let re ← bounds.BoundsError.into_range_error err
    ok (core.result.Result.Err re)
